data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 conflates evidence of a causal correction with evidence of a reliability GAIN, but they are not equivalent. The problem asks what distinguishes a genuine reliability gain from compliance that happens to track the right answer. A documented correction event (wrong pre-checklist consensus overturned by a checklist item to the correct answer) is indeed a causal signal within that single case, but a single correction does not establish a gain 'on average' or even net reliability: the same checklist could trigger more spurious reversals from-correct-to-incorrect across other cases, making net reliability unchanged or worse while still producing 'correction events' that look genuine in isolation. The target offers no criterion within a single evaluation for separating a true positive correction from a class of corrections that merely average out.
